Done. The visible suite passes.

## Root cause
`app/intervals.py` was a stub:

```python
def merge_intervals(intervals):
    return list(intervals)
```

It only shallow-copied the input — no sorting, no overlap detection, no merging — so `[(1, 3), (2, 4)]` came back unchanged instead of `[(1, 4)]`.

## File changed
- **`app/intervals.py`** (only file touched; `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 -- tests conftest.py` returns nothing, so `tests/` and `conftest.py` are untouched)

The fix sorts by `(start, end)`, merges when `start <= last_end` (so touching intervals like `(1,2),(2,3)` merge), never shrinks an interval (`if end > last_end`, so nested intervals are safe), materialises fresh tuples (no input mutation, accepts lists/tuples/generators), and returns `[]` for empty input.

## Test command run
```
/usr/local/py-utils/bin/pytest -q
```
Result: `1 passed in 0.01s`, exit code 0. Also confirmed via `/usr/local/py-utils/venvs/pytest/bin/python -m pytest -q` → same result.

Note on the environment: plain `python -m pytest -q` fails with `No module named pytest` — pytest is not installed in any of the system interpreters, and installing packages was disallowed. The pre-existing runner at `/usr/local/py-utils/bin/pytest` (a venv that already has pytest) is the working equivalent.

## Extra verification
Ran a 12-case edge-case script (empty, single, unsorted, touching, chained touching, nested, disjoint, negatives, floats, degenerate zero-width, generator input) plus a non-mutation check — all passed, output is always `list[tuple]`.

The work was done through one `spawn_subagent` call (`isolate=true, adopt=true, review_changes=true, repair_attempts=2, max_iterations=16`); its independent diff review returned PASS and the branch was merged into the parent checkout (commit `b416037`).
